description: Composite figure: a data table plus four optical micrographs (OM) of the tested low-density δ-ferrite steel rolled at four temperatures. All four OM panels are the same modality, each with a 50 μm scale bar, and all show a strongly banded (lamellar) structure; panel (a) additionally defines the rolling direction (RD, horizontal arrow) and normal direction (ND, vertical arrow). (a) R650: light δ-ferrite lamellae alternate with dark carbide/ferrite (C/F) composite lamellae, both continuously banded. (b) R750: the same δ-ferrite + C/F banding, with dark C/F bands appearing thicker/coarser. In (c) R850 and (d) R950 the dark phase is labelled Martensite and white arrows labelled "Ferrite" point to equiaxed ferrite grains enclosed within the martensite lamellae, these grains appearing much larger in (d). The table reports, for R650/R750/R850/R950, M [vol %], δ-F [vol%], C/F [vol %], carbide size [nm] and distribution density [μm-2]. It shows C/F decreasing from 51.5 ± 2.5 to 43.3 ± 3.0 vol% between 650 and 750 °C while average carbide size rises from 158.3 ± 76.9 to 247.3 ± 86.8 nm, and martensite appearing only at 850-950 °C. Together the panels argue that rolling temperature switches the lamellar structure from δ-ferrite + carbide/ferrite composite lamellae to δ-ferrite + honeycomb martensite.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph of R650 with 50 μm scale bar: alternating light δ-ferrite lamellae and dark carbide/ferrite composite lamellae, both continuously banded; RD (horizontal) and ND (vertical) arrows labelled in the upper right.

Optical micrograph of R750 with 50 μm scale bar: banded dark carbide/ferrite lamellae interleaved with light δ-ferrite lamellae; labels 'Carbide / Ferrite' on the dark bands and 'δ-Ferrite' on the light bands.

Optical micrograph of R850 with 50 μm scale bar: light δ-ferrite lamellae alternating with dark Martensite lamellae; an arrow labelled 'Ferrite' points to equiaxed ferrite grains enclosed in the martensite.
Optical micrograph of R950 with 50 μm scale bar: δ-ferrite lamellae and Martensite lamellae, with a labelled arrow pointing to Ferrite (equiaxed grains) that appear larger than in (c).

observations.observation: All four micrographs (a)-(d) carry a 50 μm scale bar and show a banded/lamellar structure.
Panel (a) labels horizontal and vertical arrows as RD and ND respectively.
In (a) and (b) the light phase is labelled 'δ-Ferrite' and the dark phase 'Carbide / Ferrite'; in (c) and (d) the light phase is 'δ-Ferrite' and the dark phase 'Martensite'.
Panels (c) and (d) contain an arrow labelled 'Ferrite' pointing to equiaxed ferrite grains enclosed within the martensite lamellae.
The caption identifies the four micrographs as OM of the tested steel: (a) R650, (b) R750, (c) R850, and (d) R950.
The table reports R650: M = 0 vol%, δ-F = 48.5 ± 2.5 vol%, C/F = 51.5 ± 2.5 vol%, carbide size = 158.3 ± 76.9 nm, distribution density = 1.7 ± 0.2 μm-2.
The table reports R750: M = 0 vol%, δ-F = 56.7 ± 3.0 vol%, C/F = 43.3 ± 3.0 vol%, carbide size = 247.3 ± 86.8 nm, distribution density = 0.6 ± 0.1 μm-2.
The table reports R850: M = 33.2 ± 3.6 vol%, δ-F = 66.8 ± 3.6 vol%, C/F = 0 vol%, with carbide size and distribution density marked '-' (not applicable).
The table reports R950: M = 59.0 ± 4.2 vol%, δ-F = 41.0 ± 4.2 vol%, C/F = 0 vol%, with carbide size and distribution density marked '-' (not applicable).
As rolling temperature increases from 650 °C to 750 °C the proportion of carbide/ferrite composite lamellae decreases from 51.5 % to 43.3 %.
As rolling temperature rises from 850 °C to 950 °C the proportion of honeycomb martensite lamellae increases from 33.2 % to 59.0 %.
Low-temperature rolling (650-750 °C) forms alternating δ-ferrite lamellae (light areas) and carbide/ferrite composite lamellae (dark areas), both continuously banded.
High-temperature rolling (850-950 °C) produces a duplex structure of δ-ferrite lamellae (light) and honeycomb martensite lamellae (dark) with equiaxed ferrite grains (DIF) enclosed in the martensite.
Equiaxed ferrite grains inside the martensite grow significantly as rolling temperature rises from 850 °C to 950 °C.

unreadable_items: Individual carbide particles inside the dark carbide/ferrite lamellae cannot be resolved at the supplied resolution and 50 μm scale
Exact equiaxed-ferrite grain sizes in (c) and (d) are not printed and cannot be measured from the images
